Ranganatha reclines on Ananta in the Kaveri island kshetra praised across Alvar hymns and Sri Vaishnava tradition. Often paired with nearby Thiruvanaikaval on Trichy pilgrimages.

Classical pilgrimage teaching places Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam within India’s tirtha network: a location where devotion to Lord Ranganatha (Vishnu reclining on Ananta) is believed to ripen vows more readily than in ordinary space. Epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya literature — not a single uniform text — sustain this sense of sacred geography.
